text:
Maya Chen: Quick design question — attaching the new autoscale panel mock. I put the SLO slider above the min/max fields and the burst toggle inline with the GPU pool selector. My concern: visually it reads as if the SLO is the primary control and capacity is secondary. Do we want that?
Samir Patel: I think capacity (min/max + pool) should be the dominant group. Users come here mainly to set limits. SLO feels like a quality guardrail, lower visual weight. Also the slider handle color fails contrast on some monitors.
Jon Reynolds: Implementation note — moving SLO around will change form layout and focus order. If it’s top-level it might get accidentally adjusted. Could we hide SLO under a collapsible "Advanced SLOs" section to reduce accidental edits?
Ava Gomez: Accessibility nit: the slider thumb has a 2.8:1 contrast ratio vs background, fails WCAG AA. We also need aria-valuetext and keyboard +/- stepper support for the slider. Right now keyboard only focuses but doesn't change value smoothly.
Maya Chen: Good points. Collapse helps prevent accidents, but PMs want SLO visible at a glance. Maybe compromise: keep SLO visible but visually de-emphasize it (lighter label, smaller track) and ensure keyboard and a11y fixes.
design-bot: Prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE — frame "autoscale_v2/slo-above" (link updated).
Samir Patel: For the burst control, inline felt discoverable but it competes with pool-level metadata. Suggest turning burst into a small secondary row under pool selector: label + toggle + "?" tooltip. Tooltip copy: "Temporarily borrows extra GPUs to handle short spikes; billed separately."
Jon Reynolds: Agree on the tooltip. Also propose a guardrail: if pool is configured as spot-preferred, disable the burst toggle and show an explanation. Backend will block incompatible combinations, but let's prevent the user flow early.
Ava Gomez: For tooltips and disabled states remember to set aria-describedby and not rely solely on color. Disabled toggles still need accessible labels and focusable help links.
Maya Chen: Copy question — do we prefer "Burst" or "Burst capacity"? Product thinks shorter is fine but it might be ambiguous.
Samir Patel: Prefer "Burst capacity" in the form, but keep the toggle labelled "Burst" for the compact card variant. Consistent tooltip explains term.
Jon Reynolds: Minor dev detail: the min/max steppers currently allow 0.1 GPU increments in the mock, but our pools are integer GPU counts. Let's constrain to integer steps and add a subtle microcopy: "rounded to whole GPUs on apply."
Ava Gomez: Keyboard compatibility: ensure steppers have aria-labels like "Min GPUs" "Max GPUs" and arrow keys change by 1.
Maya Chen: Layout iteration idea: left column = pool selector + burst toggle + min/max, right column = SLO slider + estimated latency preview + recommended config hint. That keeps capacity grouped while keeping SLO visible. Thoughts?
Samir Patel: 👍 Left grouping makes sense. The estimated latency preview might steal attention; make it visually lighter than the capacity controls.
Jon Reynolds: From the runtime side, we can provide recommended config info via an API call. Suggest the UI show a loading skeleton and avoid flashing values that move around.
Ava Gomez: Also include a text-only mode for dashboards (for screen reader users) — the preview should have an offscreen text summary: "At this configuration expected p95 latency ~ 320ms" and an aria-live region for updates.
Maya Chen: Great. Action items: 1) I’ll update mock to left-group capacity, smaller SLO styling, add tooltip copy. 2) Jon will add a note about disabling burst for spot pools and integer-only steppers. 3) Ava will provide exact a11y requirements (contrast target, aria attrs). 4) Samir will sanity-check copy tone. Back here once mocks are updated — aiming for a quick sync tomorrow. :spiral_calendar: 
Samir Patel: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
design-bot: Update: prototype comments added for a11y fixes and tooltip copy.
Maya Chen: Thanks — will post updated frames when ready.
